TLINE.TDLINE: &TITLE&
View Stored SOD Results
&PURPOSE&
The results of a specific SOD analysis are given a Result ID. This
report can show the results of a single Result ID.
&INTEGRATION&
&PREREQUISITES&
&FEATURES&
&SELECTION&
The selection screen allows you to restrict the results of a single
Result ID by Conflict, User, Cost Center, User Group, Company,
Department or Conflict Origin.
Conflict Origin: System to limit which of the conflicts that were found
in the analysis will be displayed.
Local(1)
- The user has all the functions in the conflict on the local system and
the user has no functions on any other system
Remote (2)
- The user has all the functions in the conflict on exactly 1 of the
Remote systems, and no functions on any other system
Cross (3)
- The user has functions in the conflicts on multiple systems, but on no
system has the user all of the functions
Local and Cross(4)
- The user has all the functions in the conflict on the local system.
The user has some functions in the conflicts on a remote system, but on
no remote system does the user have all the functions
Remote and Cross(5)
- The user has all the functions in the conflict on a remote system and
the user has functions in the conflicts on multiple systems, but on the
local system the user doesn't have all the functions
Local, Remote and Cross (6)
- The user has all the functions in the conflict on the local system and
the user has all the functions in the conflict on a remote system.
Filter based on origin
Local
Show the conflicts with status 1,4 and 6
Do not show conflicts with status 2,3 and 5
Remote
Show the conflicts with status 2,5 and 6
Do not show conflicts with status 1,3 and 4
Cross
Show the conflicts with status 3,4,5 and 6
Do not show conflicts with status 1 and 2
In case Store SOD Results report is run for SE version less than 4.6,
warning message ‘Conflict origin filter not supported for SOD analysis
executed in Separations Enforcer versions before 4.6’ would be displayed
in report View Stored SOD results if either of local or remote or cross
checkbox is unchecked.
In the Grouping-section, you can select how you want these results to
be grouped in the output of this report.
In the Maximum Expansion level you can select to what level the results
can be expanded and will be included in exports and downloads.
The User Selection area can be used to determine for which users you
want to see results based on wether or not they had conflicts during the
analysis.
Valid and Dialog Users Only: Fill this checkbox if you would like to
runthis analysis for currently valid (non-locked, non-expired) and
dialog users only.
<ZK>When this checkbox is checked, the Security Weaver definition will
be shown in the disabled fields: </>
User type = A
<ZU>Exclude Users:</>
Locked: This is checked to exclude locked users from the analysis.
Outside of Validity Dates (Expired/Future): This is checked to exclude
expired or future dated users from the analysis.
<ZK>When this checkbox is </><ZU>un-checked</><ZK>, these fields then
open up for entry. </>
User type: Enter the user type as you wish for selection of users.
<ZK>,,You can set the default User Type(s) for when the "Valid &
Dialog"is un-checked. </>
<ZK>,,This is set up in transaction STVARV with a Selection Option entry
named </><ZH>/PSYNG/USERTYPE</><ZK>.,,When this parameter is not set up,
it will default to A.</>
<ZU>Exclude Users:</>
Locked: Change as you wish for analysis of locked users.
Outside of Validity Dates (Expired/Future): Change as you wish for
analysis of expired/future users.
<ZK>,,You can set the defaults for these checkboxes for when the "Valid
& Dialog" is un-checked. </>
<ZK>,,This is set up in the Misc. Tab -> SE Config Parameters in </>
<ZH>DLFT_EXCLUDE_LOCKED </><ZK>and ,,</><ZH>DFLT_EXCL_OUT_VALID</><ZK>.
<ZK>Additionally, considering a user to be "locked" by their user master
status is determined by the config parameters </><ZH>
REP_USR_LOK_DSP_MGR</><ZK> and </><ZH>REP_USR_LOK_DSP_SLF</><ZK>.</>
&STANDARD_VARIANTS&
&OUTPUT&
The results will be presented in a tree format.
The first level of the tree is determined by the grouping that was
selected in the selection screen (Usergroup, Cost Center, Company or
Department)
The second level contains all users that have conflicts.
The third level contains all the conflicts.
The fourth level contains all the functions
The fifth level contains the roles or profiles causing the function.
The sixth level contains
,, The Transactions, Objects, Fields and values causing the function
,, The Org Levels the user has access to for these functions (if any)
The seventh level contains the Objects, fields and Values that give the
user access to these Org Levels
,,The Variable Elements the user has access to for these functions (if
any)
Export Options
The Output data can be exported with the three different options by
clicking on Export button.
Export Data to ALV - The output data will be displayed in ALV format.
Export Data to Local File - The output data will be exported to a Local
file. A dialog box will appear to select the File location on the Local
PC. If the number of records in the output is greater than the value of
parameter SOD_EXPORT_ALV_LIMIT, the data will be splitted into multiple
files depending upon the parameter value.
Export Data to Server - The output data will be stored on application
server path in files. Enter the Application Server path and the Batch
Size(Records). Data will be stored in the multiple files on the server
path based on the value mentioned in Batch size(Records) field. A
background job will be scheduled and store the data on server path.
Note: The server path(directory) has to be created to store the files.
